When the opposition gets hardest the results slip below average too. A developing regular who already makes fights count.

supermutant.text: SuperMutant wins the old-fashioned way: the matchup tally sits in the top shelf, and the lifetime numbers agree. Headshots are rare — that line sits near the bottom — yet the damage keeps coming, steady and unspectacular. Brave enough to hold their own as the opposition sharpens, and the tempo never lets the other side breathe. A strong regular who gets there without the highlight reel.

savalialucifica.text: SavaliaLucifica plays a bright, balanced game, in the upper reaches on nearly every count. Playing at a lively clip, and fearless as the opposition stiffens. Steady results against the hardest opposition too, barely bending when the heat rises. The head-to-head tally sits above average, and the career board tells the same story. A strong regular with no weak corner and a bright card.

sibodohyghodoh.text: SiBodohYgHodoh plays a slow, deliberate game, and it works, sitting comfortably above the middle overall. Unhurried on the tempo, and patient to a fault. The matchup ledger sits near the very top, and the resistance is top-shelf too — the fights they take, they win. Yet the lifetime IvI line sits near the bottom, and the pace is below average. A deliberate regular whose matchups and lifetime board could not disagree more.

silentneurosis.text: SilentNeurosis plays a razor-sharp game, well clear of the middle on nearly every count. Setting a brisk pace, and fearless while the opposition stiffens. The accuracy sits near the very top, while the lifetime IvI line matches it — the two brightest figures on the card. When the fights get hardest, the results slip a little, the one soft corner. A strong regular with a surgeon's aim and a fast trigger finger.

sainjtz.text: Sainjtz has been at this since 2017: sharp reflexes, level-headed as the pressure mounts, and unruffled when the fight thickens. Their head-to-head work lands mid-pack and the lifetime view sits a touch behind them. A veteran who still sets the tempo — and whose greatest strength remains showing up, fight after fight.

srarfoulaa01.text: Srarfoulaa01 never lets a fight cool down: among the bravest tracked, relentless at a high tempo, and still sharp when the fighting heats up. In head-to-head fights they clear the middle by a wide margin, and the lifetime view backs it up. A player who turns every exchange into a race — and usually wins the race.

sterikeppa.text: SterikePPA plays at full throttle: among the quickest tracked, fearless when the fight thickens, and still sharp when the fighting gets fiercest. Head-to-head, they finish well above the middle, and the lifetime view agrees with that. Resistance runs middling and the edge frays a touch against the hardest fights — but the tempo rarely gives the other side room to breathe.

shackz.text: Shackz has been a steady hand since 2014: above the pack in the matchups, comfortable as the opposition strengthens, and brisk enough to keep the tempo lively. The duel ledger lands mid-pack, but the pace and the pressure stay above the middle, and the lifetime board paints a similar middle-to-strong picture. A long-serving regular who makes every fight honest work.

shikinamiasukarangure.text: ShikinamiAsukaRangure brings a brisk, well-rounded approach: above average in the matchups, at ease as the opposition strengthens, and brisk on the move. The duel ledger rests mid-pack, but the pace, the accuracy, and the lifetime board all run above average. A strong regular with no obvious hole, the kind who makes every fight a grind for the other side.

sousoufar.text: SOUSOUFAR has only just arrived, and already the opening pages turn heads: above average in the matchups, calm as the opposition strengthens, and remarkably steady in the hardest fights. The head-to-head ledger sits near the very best, though the aim is still loose and headshots are scarce. Brand new, so this is an early read, but the first impression is a strong one.

skycrazypotato.text: Since 2015, Skycrazypotato has been the matchup board's quiet surprise: well above average overall, difficult to unseat in a straight fight, and unmoved when the opposition gets strongest. The form barely wobbles against the toughest foes, a steady hand in a long career. Most fights end with the matchup count tipping their way. The all-time ledger undersells the whole picture, with the all-time IvI line sitting below the middle, but this veteran wins by picking the right moments.

splatterdevil.text: Splatterdevil has been around since 2012, and the long career shows in a calm, picky approach: they take fights they can win and walk away from the rest with a better exchange than most. Accuracy and headshots sit below the middle, so the edge comes from judgment, not raw aim. Against the very best opposition the results soften, but the instincts stay sharp.

stooneytr.text: StooneyTR thrives on tempo, pressing the fight with a pace that lands well above the usual and holding their ground as the enemy quality climbs. Their staying power dips a little against the hardest opposition, and over a full career the picture is a touch more modest than the recent duels. Steady aim and a brisk rhythm make them a reliable presence wherever the fighting thickens.

skrock1234.text: Skrock1234 plays a brisk, even game: well above average through most of the shape, quick to every exchange, and steady when the fighting hardens. The head-to-head results sit mid-pack, a notch below the rest of the shape, while the pace and the pressure carry the day. The lifetime board lands in the middle too, which keeps the story honest: a strong regular with no glaring hole.

slayer666il7.text: SLAYER666IL7 has been fighting since 2014, and the lifetime kill-death picture sits near the very top — more kills than deaths by a wide margin. The aim is loose, headshots are scarce, and the heaviest fighting wears the edge down fast. Yet the head-to-head exchanges stay well above average, built on nerve and positioning rather than marksmanship. A veteran regular whose results outrun the raw shooting.

scgfear.text: ScgFear attacks every fight at full tilt: well above average in the matchups, fast on their feet, and quick to press any opening. The momentum stalls against the fiercest opposition, where the results go quiet. The lifetime figures sit a touch below the matchup return, which keeps the story honest: a fierce regular with one clear ceiling.

suilean.text: Suilean brings a complete game with one sharp edge: well above average almost everywhere, and the aim sits among the very best tracked. The matchup kill-death return lands mid-pack, an honest wrinkle in an otherwise strong profile, while the lifetime figures run a touch more modest than the matchups. Quick-handed, steady against stronger opposition, and always in the fight.

sunny6666.text: Sunny6666 plays a bright, opportunistic game: well above average in the matchups, with headshots landing more often than most. The edge crumbles when the opposition gets hardest, where the results fall away quickly. The lifetime figures lean a touch stronger than the matchup return, so the story is a sharp finisher still learning how to hold up under the heaviest fire.

solarls.text: SOLARlS plays a measured game that keeps paying off: well above average overall, hard to put down, and steady even when the fight turns against them. In direct exchanges they hold their own without dominating, while the lifetime tally runs a little hotter than the matchups. Shots land where they count more often than most, and the headshots keep coming. A dependable regular whose quiet consistency does the talking.

squarelar.text: Squarelar is the kind of regular who never makes noise and never goes away: a cut above the average, hard to shift, and calm when the fight turns. Duel by duel they edge ahead of the pack, with the lifetime tally running just behind. The headshots rarely arrive and the lifetime IvI sits low, but neither gap has slowed them down. A quiet presence who keeps turning up and keeps winning more than they lose.

squaresarered.text: SquaresAreRed thrives when the fight gets crowded, sitting a clear step above the average, braver as the opposition gets stronger, and never lets the pressure drop. The lifetime board paints a more middling picture than the matchups deserve, with the pace and the staying power both running hot. In single duels they split the difference with the pack, neither giving ground nor taking much. A busy regular who makes every engagement cost something.

sysop1.text: Sysop1 has been picking fights with a jeweller's eye since 2013: well above average overall, with matchup results near the very top. The accuracy runs true, the pace stays measured, and the lifetime tally matches the matchups. But the bravery runs near the bottom, and against the hardest opposition the whole game comes apart. A veteran who wins the fights they choose and quietly skips the rest.

secretarybootyjuice.text: SecretaryBootyJuice wins the fights in front of them in style: well above average overall, a matchup record near the top, and lifetime kill-death figures to match. Accuracy sits below the middle, headshots are rare, and the lifetime IvI line sits near the bottom. When the going gets hardest, the touch fades — the one wrinkle in a loud, lively game.

shekelbot.text: Shekelbot plays a balanced game with no glaring hole: well above average overall, steady against stronger opposition, and hard to wear down in a straight exchange. The matchup record lands squarely in the middle; the lifetime figures echo that same steadiness. A dependable regular who turns up, holds the line, and makes every fight a fair one.

steelsent.text: SteelSent is barely two weeks into the game and already playing above the middle: well above average overall, a lively tempo, with a matchup record that holds up as the opposition strengthens. The lifetime figures rest in the middle so far, which is normal for a fresh account still building its history. Early days, but the opening pages carry real promise.

scorven.text: Scorven has been around since 2017, and the game still suits them: well above average in sum, with staying power above the middle and a matchup record in the upper range. The pace runs ordinary, and the accuracy rests below average, the one soft spot. The lifetime marks confirm the matchups, painting a steady veteran who wins by reading the fight rather than rushing it.

snctm.text: SNCTM plays the long game: well above average overall, with resistance that clears mid-pack, and lifetime marks that echo the matchups. The pace runs middle-of-the-pack, and the matchup record ordinary, but the aim stays true as the opposition hardens, and headshots land above average. A patient regular whose best quality is refusing to fade when the fight gets hard.

somnia335.text: Somnia335 brings energy to every fight: well above average in the round, with a brisk tempo, bravery that grows as the opposition hardens, and resistance well clear of mid-pack. The matchup tally rests above average too, while the accuracy and headshots stay middling. The spark dims a touch against the fiercest opposition, the lone wrinkle in a lively, all-round game. A regular who makes every exchange feel faster.

skdaks011.text: skdaks011 shoots like the range never closes: well above average across the picture, with accuracy up among the very best tracked and a lifetime IvI line sitting top shelf. They move at a brisk tempo and stay steady when the enemies get stronger. Yet the kill-death tally stalls mid-pack, and the toughest third eats into the results. A strong regular whose aim writes checks the tally has not cashed yet.

snotdztr.text: SnotdzTR wins ugly and wins often: well above average overall, with a lifetime kill-death line above the middle and a hide thick enough to shrug off punishment. The aim is wild — accuracy near the very bottom, but the tally still lands above the middle in the matchups. The toughest third takes a visible toll, the one soft spot in a sturdy picture. A regular who proves that placement matters less than persistence.

stary1234.text: Stary1234 is the steady middle of the game: well above average overall, patient on the trigger, and calm when the field gets tougher. They endure punishment better than most, though the toughest third eats into the tally. The aim sits below average and the returns land mid-pack — nothing flashy, just a regular who keeps showing up and keeps the fight honest.
